in_hebrew.name: שנבלט
in_hebrew.meaning: שם שנבלט נגזר משורש שבלט והוא מתורגם לאחד ששונו הבלט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שנבלט מורכב משני שורשים עבריים: 'שנ' ו'בלט'. השורש 'שנ' מתורגם לשינוי או להחלפה, והשורש 'בלט' מתורגם לבלטות או להתנשאות. לכן, ניתן לפרש את השם שנבלט כ'אחד ששונו הבלט' או 'המובלט'.

in_greek.name: Σανβαλλᾶτ
in_greek.meaning: Σανβαλλᾶτ σημαίνει αλλαγή ή μετάλλαξη και ανάδειξη
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σανβαλλᾶτ προέρχεται από δύο εβραϊκές ρίζες: 'שנ' και 'בלט'. Η ρίζα 'שנ' σημαίνει αλλαγή ή μεταβολή, ενώ η ρίζα 'בלט' σημαίνει ανάδειξη ή εξέλιξη. Συνεπώς, το όνομα Σανβαλλᾶτ μπορεί να ερμηνευτεί ως 'εκείνος που έχει αλλάξει' ή 'ο αναδειχθείς'.

in_latin.name: Sanballat
in_latin.meaning: Sanballat means change or transformation and elevation
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Sanballat is derived from two Hebrew roots: 'שנ' and 'בלט'. The root 'שנ' translates to change or transformation, while the root 'בלט' means elevation or prominence. Hence, Sanballat can be interpreted as 'one who has changed' or 'the elevated one'.

in_english.name: Sanballat
in_english.long_meaning: The name Sanballat originates from Hebrew roots 'שנ' (change or transformation) and 'בלט' (elevation or prominence). It appears in the Bible (Nehemiah 2:10, 19; 3:33; 4:1; 6:1, 14; 13:23) as the name of a Samaritan leader who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. In Christian tradition, Sanballat symbolizes opposition to spiritual growth and transformation.

biblical_reference.note: Sanballat was a Samaritan leader who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

data.cultural_impact: Sanballat is best remembered from the Old Testament as a high-ranking official in the Persian Empire during the time of Nehemiah. He is depicted as being against the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and encouraging opposition to the Jewish return from exile. Sanballat represents the challenges faced by the Jews in their attempt to restore their homeland and rebuild their Temple.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Sanballat can symbolize the internal struggles we all face in our spiritual journeys. Like the Jewish people in the time of Nehemiah, we may encounter opposition and adversity as we strive to build our spiritual lives and stay true to our beliefs. However, just as Nehemiah and his people remained steadfast in their mission, we too can overcome these challenges and transform our circumstances into opportunities for growth and spiritual refinement. In this way, the name Sanballat can serve as a reminder to stay focused on our goals and trust in the divine process of transformation.
